clue.text: Moves moderately fast for a revolutionary group

definitions.meaning: a horse that goes at a pace between walking and cantering does this
informal plural for followers of Leon Trotsky, the Russian revolutionary

explanation.surface: Someone describes a brisk pace suitable for a band of revolutionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one spelling: the verb for a jogging gait and the slang plural for Trotskyists.

clue.text: One using a slide when playing

definitions.text: One using a slide when playing

parts.words: One using a slide when playing
parts.note: reads like a child in a playground, but describes a brass player moving the instrument's sliding tube

explanation.definitionFit: A brass player whose instrument changes pitch by means of a sliding tube.

clue.text: Start of race cancelled

explanation.surface: The start of the race has been called off.
explanation.definitionFit: The same small word marks a race's beginning and an event that will not happen.

clue.text: Artist's following pupils

definitions.meaning: a group of painters sharing a master's style or approach
a body of students taught together

explanation.surface: A painter's devotees are his students.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a group of artists following one master and an institution full of students.

clue.text: Grumble, bitter about twopence for sour fruit

parts.note: to crab is to complain or grumble

indicators.note: about tells us the word for bitter goes round the twopence

parts.note: bitter is a type of British ale
P is a penny, so two of them make PP

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling and bitter over paying twopence for a tart fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: BITTER is a hoppy British draught beer; 'Grumble' and 'bitter' both read as moods, hiding their roles as synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wild apple, notably tart, used for jelly.

clue.text: Study precise limit

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
strict means exact or precise

explanation.surface: Learning exact boundaries.
explanation.definitionFit: To squeeze or restrict, keeping within narrow bounds.

clue.text: A simple-sounding Arab ruler

indicators.note: sounding tells us the phrase meaning a simple is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a mere, meaning nothing more than, simple

explanation.surface: A modest-sounding Middle Eastern leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant spelling of emir, a Muslim prince or commander.

clue.text: Name-dropping story about dress

indicators.note: dropping tells us the abbreviation for name is let fall from the story word

parts.note: an account is a story or report
RE means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A gossipy tale about clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name-dropping' suggests boasting about acquaintances; it means remove N from ACCOUNT, leaving ACCOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip or clothe, especially in military gear.

clue.text: Mix sling first — sweetheart wants a mineral

indicators.note: first tells us the throw word goes ahead of the mix word

parts.note: to sling is to pitch or throw
to blend is to mix
the heart of the word sweet is its letter E

explanation.surface: A recipe: combine a sling cocktail first, and a lover needs a mineral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' gives E, the central letter of 'sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: A uranium ore, the source from which radium was first extracted.

clue.text: In limited edition, finally published a collection of poems

parts.note: edition cut short to its abbreviation ED

indicators.note: finally tells us to take the closing letter of the word published

explanation.surface: In a small print run, a poetry anthology finally came out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edda is a medieval Icelandic compilation of Norse mythological verse.

clue.text: Remote possibility of a catch in the slips?

definitions.meaning: a slim likelihood that something may happen
in cricket the slips stand on the off side, so a chance there is a chance on the off

explanation.surface: A cricket fan muses on the slim hope of a catch among the slip fielders.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the slips are fielders behind the batsman on the off side; a catching opportunity is called a chance, so a slip catch is literally an off chance.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a slight likelihood, said of something unlikely but worth trying for.

clue.text: Quoted saw in speech

indicators.note: in speech tells us the word for saw is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to have sighted something is to have seen or saw it

explanation.surface: Someone quoted an old proverb, a saw, while talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a noun (a saying), which suits 'Quoted', but it is the past of see.
explanation.definitionFit: To have referred to a source or passage is to have quoted it, as in court or an essay.

clue.text: Provided with front fastenings, but not turned and finished

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turned tells us the word not is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
to be through is to be finished, done with

explanation.surface: A garment had fasteners at the front but was never turned and completed.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a dress or skirt fastened by a row of buttons running all the way down the front.

clue.text: Women with wills of their own

definitions.text: Women with wills of their own

parts.words: Women with wills of their own
parts.note: reads as headstrong women, but means women who have made legal wills

explanation.definitionFit: The feminine plural of the legal term for those who have made a will.

clue.text: Security zone in which one can travel with less risk

definitions.meaning: safety means security and a belt is a zone or strip

definitions.text: in which one can travel with less risk
definitions.meaning: the strap worn in a car to protect passengers

explanation.surface: A protected area where travel is less dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap in a vehicle restraining the passenger, read also as a zone of safety.

clue.text: Catch about second home

indicators.note: about tells us the word for catch goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: to net a fish is to catch it

explanation.surface: Someone catches sight of a second house.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's dwelling, and by extension any snug home.

clue.text: Family drudge who had a fit eventually

definitions.meaning: the stepdaughter in the fairy tale who does all the household chores
in the fairy tale the glass slipper finally fits her foot

explanation.surface: A put-upon household servant eventually loses her temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had a fit' suggests a tantrum; it means the slipper fitted her.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale heroine is the archetypal overworked servant whose foot matched the prince's slipper.

clue.text: Speak disparagingly of low degree

parts.note: down means low, depressed
a grade is a level or degree

explanation.surface: Belittling someone with a poor qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower in rank or esteem, to belittle or disparage.

clue.text: Food without flavour brought up — it's become stale

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up tells us the assembly is read from bottom to top
without here means outside, so the food word goes round the flavour word

parts.note: eats is informal for food
tang is a sharp flavour

explanation.surface: Tasteless food was regurgitated because it had gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking; the container gives ETANGATS, which 'brought up' turns over. 'brought up' suggests vomiting.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop flowing or developing, and so go foul or lifeless.

clue.text: Sea air won't upset poor community

parts.note: a sea shanty is a sailors' song, an air of the sea

indicators.note: upset tells us the letters of won't are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe giving no letter

explanation.surface: A sailor's song refuses to trouble a deprived neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea air' suggests a breeze; it is a sailors' song. 'upset' rearranges WONT to TOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement of crude shacks on a city's edge, where very poor people live.

clue.text: Keen to bust low-down joint

indicators.note: to bust is to break, so the letters of keen are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone eager to wreck a seedy dive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low-down joint' suggests a seedy bar; it is a body joint low on the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The hinge joint in the leg, lower down the body than hip.

clue.text: Liner that holds record

definitions.meaning: a tube or casing fitted inside another as a lining
the card cover a vinyl disc is kept in

explanation.surface: An ocean liner holds a speed record.
explanation.definitionFit: The protective cover in which a gramophone disc is stored.

clue.text: Mugs providing guide to form

definitions.meaning: mug shots, police photographs of faces
a police reference collection for those with a criminal record, or form

explanation.surface: Gullible people offer tips on horse-racing form.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, having 'form' means having a criminal record, and a mug is a face.
explanation.definitionFit: The police collection of photographs of known criminals, used to identify suspects.

clue.text: Serial killer, so to speak, therefore gets time

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore

explanation.surface: A murderer gets a prison sentence as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'serial killer' is 'cereal killer': ergot is a fungus that attacks rye and other cereals.
explanation.definitionFit: A fungal disease of grain crops, a destroyer of cereals.

clue.text: One of the colours carried by recruit

indicators.note: carried by tells us the letters are held within the word recruit

explanation.surface: A soldier's new recruit bears the regimental colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colours' suggests regimental flags; it means shades.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale greyish-yellow or beige shade, like unbleached linen.

clue.text: Clown with a drink

parts.note: Coco was a famous circus clown

explanation.surface: A circus clown enjoys a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: Coco the Clown was a celebrated performer in Britain's Bertram Mills Circus.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot beverage made from powdered cacao beans, often taken at bedtime.

clue.text: Bush telegraph used in midnight exercise in steep valley

parts.note: the middle of the word night is its letter G

indicators.note: in tells us the exercise letters sit inside the valley word

parts.note: a ravine is a narrow, steep-sided valley
PE, physical education, is school exercise

explanation.surface: Rumour has it some midnight training was done in a gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' gives the middle letter of 'night'. 'Bush telegraph' is informal for the rumour network.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal phrase for the unofficial spreading of rumour and gossip by word of mouth.

clue.text: Execution in the republic producing anger

indicators.note: an execution is a beheading, so the first letter is cut off

parts.note: Eire, the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland

explanation.surface: An execution in a republic causes outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Execution' means beheading: take the head (first letter) off EIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrath, a literary word for rage.

clue.text: International organisation he hates being ordered to pull out

parts.note: UN, the United Nations

indicators.note: being ordered tells us the letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man at the United Nations is told to withdraw from what he loathes.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a sword or knife from its scabbard is to pull it out.

clue.text: Having equal scores before extra time in sporting contest

indicators.note: before tells us the equal-scores word goes ahead of the time letter

parts.note: level or drawn, with equal points
T is the abbreviation for time, here added as an extra

explanation.surface: A match is level going into extra time.
explanation.definitionFit: A single competition within a programme of sport, such as a race.
